limitations: One function, unpublished version, Python 3.12, same-account standard SQS targets; no aliases, provisioned concurrency, quota changes, or account ownership inference.
Consumer absence is bounded to actual receive windows and retained runtime logs, not an assertion about infinite future behavior.
CloudWatch can lag beyond the bounded ingestion windows; absent datapoints are not synthesized zeros.
Configurations use MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=3600 and MaximumRetryAttempts=2 to distinguish immediate zero-reservation discard from the existing 60-second age exhaustion capture.

Held execution continuity is directly observed, but warm-environment reuse across subsequent reservation-only changes was not isolated: route configuration updates occurred before recovery calls, which used a different log stream. Do not infer reservation changes redeploy code.

documentation.relevant_contract: Reserved concurrency is a cap and reservation; zero intentionally throttles; leave 100 unreserved.
At reserved zero, new async events go to DLQ or failure destination without retries.
Throttles are not Invocations or Errors; dropped async includes reserved zero.
Function-level concurrency throttle reason; DryRun validates request and permission, status 204.

findings.dry_run: All three DryRun calls returned 204 despite occupied reserved-one capacity or reserved zero; no corresponding runtime audit or log entry.

active_reservation_changes.result: Put(0), Delete, Put(1) all completed while the same invocation remained active. It subsequently consumed the owned release signal and returned success. Get after Delete was an empty object, not ReservedConcurrentExecutions:0.

zero_reservation.legacy_ErrorMessage: Function not invoked. Function isconfigured with zero reserved concurrent executions
zero_reservation.legacy_payload_bytes: All legacy receipt bodies exactly match original invocation payload bytes, including leading space, Unicode, and trailing newline.
zero_reservation.both_routes: Both configured routes each received both submitted events; no exclusive destination-over-DLQ precedence observed. Isolated configurations delivered only to their configured target within bounded observation windows.
zero_reservation.distinction: Unlike prior held-reserved-one EventAgeExceeded(count 0), zero reservation omits even the 429 responseContext and DLQ ErrorCode. Unlike ordinary RetriesExhausted, customer code never ran.

findings.recovery: Fresh synchronous and asynchronous submissions entered and exited the real runtime after restoring one unit; no previously discarded zero-reservation label appeared in audit receipts or captured runtime logs.
findings.metric_distinctions: Final native Errors sum 0 has SampleCount 7, while Invocations sum/SampleCount are 4. Throttles sum 3 has SampleCount 7. AsyncEventsDropped sum 4 has SampleCount 5, retaining the successful async zero sample. Neither delivery-failure metric had datapoints; this is missing, not a measured zero.
